item.title: Modernize Databases Faster with AI-Assisted Migration and Optimization — Tue Oct 27, 1:00 PM
item.description:
Microsoft Reactor Toronto Database modernization has never had a magic button. Migrations can take weeks or months of converting code, resolving incompatibilities, and validating that applications still work as expected. AI is changing that. In this session, we’ll use Visual Studio Code, Microsoft Foundry, and GitHub Copilot to accelerate an end-to-end migration to PostgreSQL on Azure HorizonDB.
We’ll assess the existing application, convert schemas and SQL code, fix migration gaps, and progressively validate data, application logic, business behavior, and workloads.
Through a practical, end-to-end migration, we’ll show how AI can accelerate database modernization and help teams migrate faster and with greater confidence.
--------------------------------------------------------
Check out the series - https://aka.ms/ModernizefasteSeries
[eventID:27666]
Source: Meetup: Microsoft Reactor Toronto

item.title: NEW EVENT - 👻🌙 The Ghosts of Cabbagetown — Tue Oct 27, 6:30 PM
item.description:
Toronto Movies & Social Group - Celebrating 14 Years! # 👻🌙 The Ghosts of Cabbagetown
### A 90-Minute Evening Ghost Walk Through One of Toronto’s Most Historic Neighbourhoods
Cabbagetown has beautiful Victorian houses, quiet streets, old cemeteries, and a history that goes back generations. It also has ghosts.
Join me for a **90-minute evening walking tour through Cabbagetown**, where we'll explore some of the neighbourhood's strangest stories, unsettling legends, and darker pieces of Toronto's past.
We'll begin beneath the glass of **Allan Gardens**, then make our way through the streets of Cabbagetown, stopping along the way for stories of mysterious creatures, haunted buildings, old prisons, cemeteries, restless spirits, and the people who may never have quite left. This isn't a traditional history walk.

item.title: Moonlight Hike - Ajax Waterfront — Tue Oct 27, 7:00 PM
item.description:
GTA Hiking & Stuff Join us for our second moonlight hike of the season. We plan to post hikes throughout the year during the nights around the full moon. These hikes are all about the energy of the moon. We can share interesting facts about that months full moon.
We will hike at a easy pace doing 5 - 6 km in 2 hrs or less. Please bring a headlamp or a flashlight.
This month we will walk the path along the Ajax waterfront. Watching the moon rise over **Lake Ontario** is quite the experience. The moon looks bigger when it rises because of a trick of perception known as the Moon illusion. Since there will be no obstructions at the waterfront we can put this illusion to the test.
Let's hope it will be clear so we can see the sun at night. The moon can get bright enough to turn off our headlamps while we hike so, if you haven't experienced a night hike, come out and enjoy the adventure. Just don't be the last in line.😬
**Note**
- Arrive on time! Please cancel if you can't make it. - Kn

item.title: Nov 9 - Agentic Labeling for Specialized Visual Data — Mon Nov 9, 12:00 PM
item.description:
Toronto AI, Machine Learning and Computer Vision Meetup **Date, Time and Location**
Nov 09, 2026 9:00 AM - 10:00 AM PST Online. **[Register for the Zoom!](https://voxel51.com/events/when-prompting-beats-training-agentic-labeling-for-specialized-visual-data-november-9-2026)**
Frontier multimodal models handle familiar concepts well and struggle on niche ones: sorting drill-core samples into 35 geological classes, or telling adhesion from scarring on a ceramic substrate. Our study across 11 specialized visual datasets in manufacturing inspection, geology, and medical imaging found that a few labeled examples in the prompt can close much of that gap, and it also found where that stops working.
**What you’ll learn:**
* Niche versus hard: how in-context examples supply domain knowledge a model is missing, and how to tell a niche task from a genuinely hard one * What the study measured: on an industrial defect task, one labeled example per class raised macro-F1 from 34% to 59% with no fi
